findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the truncation branch detects a provider_details-only length/max_tokens signal (not just the normalized finish_reason) so it reclassifies to the concision ModelRetry rather than falling through to check_response's terminal path.
evidence: Plan step 2(a): truncation subset detection is via check_stop_reason on the resolved reason; step 2(b) delegates the non-truncation path to check_response which raises terminal UnretryableOutputError for max_tokens/length.
structured.py:645-646: check_stop_reason only raises on the normalized stop_reason argument, so a None/stop-normalized turn passes it.
structured.py:672-678: check_response treats a raw provider_details finish_reason in _UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS (which includes length/max_tokens) as terminal UnretryableOutputError.
findings.finding: For a truncation that surfaces ONLY in provider_details (normalized finish_reason None/stop, raw provider finish_reason length/max_tokens — the #5221 shape S1 explicitly guards), the plan's truncation->concision-ModelRetry branch keyed off check_stop_reason will miss it, so the delegate branch's check_response raises a TERMINAL UnretryableOutputError instead of the bounded concision retry the contract promises.
findings.location: Approach step 2(a)/(b) and Acceptance Criteria line 5 ('length/max_tokens consumes at most the configured output-retry allowance ...')
scenarios: A provider/adapter that leaves finish_reason unmapped but records raw length/max_tokens in provider_details truncates the response — plan intends a concision retry, but the run terminates.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the guard classify truncation off BOTH the normalized finish_reason and the raw provider_details finish_reason (the same length/max_tokens membership check_response uses) before delegating, so any truncation shape maps to the bounded concision ModelRetry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite the specific pydantic-ai mechanism (e.g., the per-output-type retries budget / retries={'output': allowance}) that guarantees concision ModelRetry and parse/validation ModelRetry share ONE counter, resolving the upstream 'layers don't share budgets' caution.
evidence: Plan: 'Output-size (concision) and parse/validation retries draw from the SAME counter — structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES (=2)'

Retrieved pydantic-ai retries doc (github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/retries.md): "'Retry' means five different things in an agent run, at five different layers, and they don't share budgets. Mixing them up is the usual cause of a run that retries far more (or far less) than expected."

This is a load-bearing capability claim: the shared-counter behavior is the crux of AC5 ('consumes at most the configured output-retry allowance (shared with parse/validation retries; not a separate counter)')
findings.finding: Item 3 asserts that output-size (concision) ModelRetry and parse/validation ModelRetry draw from the SAME shared counter (structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES) under one UsageLimits.request_limit, but does not cite the pydantic-ai mechanism that guarantees both kinds of ModelRetry share a single per-output-type retry budget rather than being counted as distinct retry layers.
findings.location: Approach item 3 ("One shared request budget, one shared retry counter") and AC line 5
scenarios: A truncation-driven concision ModelRetry and a validation-driven ModelRetry occur in the same run and the framework counts them against separate budgets, so the run retries more than the intended OUTPUT_RETRIES=2 units
Reviewer cannot confirm the 2x-B inverse and exhaustion behavior hold without knowing the retry budgets are actually unified
findings.suggested_fix: In item 3 (or the pai_retry.py docstring derivation), name the pydantic-ai retry layer both ModelRetry kinds resolve to (the output-type retry budget wired via retries={'output': allowance}), and add a focused test asserting a concision retry and a validation retry in the same run jointly draw from the single OUTPUT_RETRIES allowance.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify HOW the operation guard distinguishes the truncation subset (length/max_tokens) from the terminal refusal/content_filter subset given both share _UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS and UnretryableOutputError — e.g. read the normalized finish_reason directly (plus the provider_details raw finish_reason) rather than via check_stop_reason's raise, and correct the plan's claim that check_stop_reason normalizes provider_details.
evidence: Plan: 'it resolves the reason through the SAME shared classifier (structured.check_stop_reason, which normalizes finish_reason and the raw provider_details two-layer shape), and when that reason is the truncation subset (length/max_tokens) raises ... ModelRetry'
structured.py:635-648 check_stop_reason(stop_reason: str|None)->None RAISES; inspects only finish_reason
structured.py:651-679 check_response reads provider_details (the two-layer shape), not check_stop_reason
structured.py:632 _UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS = frozenset({refusal, max_tokens, length, content_filter}) — truncation and refusal/content_filter share one set and one exception type
findings.finding: The plan describes the truncation guard as resolving the stop reason through `structured.check_stop_reason` 'which normalizes finish_reason AND the raw provider_details two-layer shape,' but the code shows check_stop_reason takes only finish_reason and RAISES (it does not return a reason), while the provider_details two-layer logic lives in check_response. Both the truncation subset (length/max_tokens) and the terminal subset (refusal/content_filter) map to the SAME _UNRETRYABLE_STOP_REASONS frozenset and raise the SAME UnretryableOutputError type, so the guard cannot separate 'reclassify to concision ModelRetry' from 'stay terminal' via the shared classifier as described without either reading the reason directly or modifying the shared tables (which the plan forbids).
scenarios: A max_tokens truncation must become a bounded concision ModelRetry
A refusal/content_filter must stay terminal with no retry

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the claim that the after_model_request concision ModelRetry and the TextOutput output-function ModelRetry decrement the SAME pydantic-ai 'output' retry counter (cite the counter-selection wiring), or revise step 3 to describe the actual shared-budget enforcement mechanism.
evidence: Plan: 'Output-size (concision) and parse/validation retries draw from the SAME counter — structured.OUTPUT_RETRIES (=2) ... not a separate budget. A single truncation spends one unit'
S1 wires the parse retry via TextOutput output_function (pai_output.py:36-55); the concision retry is a NEW after_model_request guard (pai_retry) attached instead of guard_capability
The plan cites no pydantic-ai mechanism proving both ModelRetry sites decrement the same 'output' counter; the library is out of the repo file tools' reach and this is a load-bearing internal
findings.finding: The plan asserts that output-size (concision) retries raised in the operation's after_model_request guard and parse/validation retries raised in the TextOutput output function draw from the SAME retries={'output': allowance} counter, but does not ground this in pydantic-ai's retry-counter wiring. A ModelRetry raised from a model-request capability hook and one raised from an output-validator function may be tracked by different retry counters; if so, the 'one shared retry counter' guarantee and the exhaustion-to-UnexpectedModelBehavior behavior do not hold.
findings.location: Approach step 3 (one shared retry counter) / Acceptance Criteria #5 and #7
scenarios: Repeated concision failures interleaved with parse failures must exhaust ONE shared budget of 2
Exhaustion must raise UnexpectedModelBehavior for translation to UnretryableOutputError

findings.finding: The subject plan's guard composition contradicts the prerequisite's stated attachment seam for the stop/refusal safety hook. The prerequisite S1 specifies the guard is delivered as a `pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability` attached via `Agent(..., capabilities=[cap])` (an `after_model_request` capability), and it exposes `pai_output.guard_capability()`. The subject plan describes attaching its concision-aware guard 'INSTEAD OF `pai_output.guard_capability()`' but also states `pai_retry` 'supplies its own `after_model_request` capability' — consistent as a capability. However, the subject plan additionally claims the S1 guard has a 'terminal-truncation contract' where `length`/`max_tokens` is terminal, whereas the prerequisite S1 explicitly states its guard raises the terminal `UnretryableOutputError` for 'refusal / `max_tokens` / `length` / `content_filter`'. The subject then treats the S1 guard as reclassifying only refusal/content_filter as terminal while subject handles truncation separately — this is a faithful override, but the subject's description of what S1 delegates ('re-raise terminal `UnretryableOutputError` (refusal/`content_filter`)') omits that S1's `check_response`/guard also treats `length`/`max_tokens` as terminal `UnretryableOutputError`, which the subject's delegated `structured.check_response` call would still raise as terminal — conflicting with the subject's intent to intercept truncation before delegation.
